summary.prose: Building this Story is seven small, strictly-ordered edits across two packages, not one large change. The daemon side is a single additive widening; the client side mirrors it as pass-through; then a pure, headlessly-testable function supplies section identity before anything consumes it; then the body render switches to the guarded markdown path in one atomic change with the contract test that protects it; and finally the index is posted and the chooser wired. Every task is S-sized, each lands with its own tests, and the riskiest moment — swapping the render and narrowing the surface's only mechanical guard — is deliberately one admission rather than two. NOTE on vocabulary: the LLD's test strategy uses a `contract` level that this plan's schema does not offer, so those are recorded here as `unit`, which is what they are mechanically — node:test assertions over the generated shell and the projected view, with no runner change.

tasks.title: Render the body through the guarded markdown path, publish StructuredRenderer, and narrow the shell contract test — one atomic change
tasks.summary: Replace `bodyEl.textContent=m.markdown||''` at docs-review-panel.ts:186 with the guarded render: prepend MARKED_SRC into the EXISTING single nonce'd script tag at :210 (mirroring chat-panel.ts:561, which interpolates `${MARKED_SRC}\n;${bootstrap}`), then run parse, then guardMd, then textContent-on-throw. MarkdownBodyRenderer returns { el, degradation } per the ratified widening, not the HLD sketch's bare HTMLElement. ALSO publish StructuredRenderer here — the sc2 type s2/s3/s4 build their renderers against; s1 declares it and implements none. In the SAME task, narrow the shell contract test: drop the blanket assert.doesNotMatch at docs-review-panel.test.ts:253, add an assert-the-guard-is-present assertion per the chat-panel.test.ts precedent, keep the one-script / CSP / surface-class assertions, add no-remote-origin, and RENAME the test to describe what it now checks. REVISED per critique: slug stamping moved out to t6 (nothing before t6 reads the slugs), which drops this task from M to S. The render and the test narrowing stay together because splitting them leaves either a red suite or an unguarded surface. REVISED per the plan review (HIGH-1): this task also owns the container and the stylesheet the rendered markup needs, because without them the render swap is invisible as an improvement. The body element today is `<pre id="insrc-docs-body" class="insrc-docs-content">` at docs-review-panel.ts:206 and NO CSS rule for .insrc-docs-content exists anywhere, so it carries the UA default white-space:pre and a monospace font; marked emits newline-separated block elements, so parsed markdown would render with a literal blank line between every block and monospace headings. Swap the <pre> for a non-preformatted container (nothing but bodyEl reads it, so the change is local) and add the markdown element rules this surface needs. The shell's only stylesheet is renderTerminalStyle (design-tokens.ts:174), which emits CSS custom properties and surface classes and NO element rules; the .insrc-md stylesheet that makes the chat surface legible lives in chat-panel.ts / render-registry.ts, which this shell does not include — so the rules must be added here rather than imported.

tasks.title: Post the section index and degradation on the existing docs-content message
tasks.summary: Append two optional members — sections and degradation — to the existing docs-content variant in protocol.ts (six members at :57-63) and post them from openDoc alongside the content. No new message TYPE: the name list at protocol.ts:117 is untouched and the webview's single message handler keeps its existing switch. The host computes the index once per opened document rather than per interaction. REVISED per the plan review (HIGH-2): the LLD's test-strategy item for this task presumes the pane's monotonic refresh guard protects the opened-document path. It does not. refreshSeq is declared at docs-review-panel.ts:66 and checked at :75/:78/:83, all three inside refreshPending(), which posts the docs-LIST — the source comment at :63-65 says exactly that. openDoc(), the function that awaits client.content() and posts the docs-content message this task extends, takes no sequence number and does no supersede check. So this task asserts the invariant that IS true and is the one the reviewer depends on: the sections index and the markdown it was derived from ride ONE message, so a superseded open swaps both together and a stale index can never be paired with newer markdown. The pre-existing openDoc race — two quick opens with the first IPC slower will display the wrong document entirely — is a real defect but is NOT introduced by this Story and is NOT in its scope; it is recorded here so it is filed as its own tracked bugfix rather than absorbed into this task or papered over by a test that measures refreshPending instead.

tasks.summary: REVISED per critique: retitled and reduced from a verify-everything catch-all to the only two checks that genuinely cannot be done earlier.
